chunks: 8 – al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī ʿUthmān, Abū Muḥammad, called al-Sajjāda, al-Qummī. Weak. In his madhhab there is irtifāʿ.

key_terms.ارْتِفَاعٌ: Elevation / Exaltation (a technical term in rijal indicating a narrator's beliefs are slightly elevated or distinct, often implying minor deviation or uniqueness)
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak (in terms of hadith narrator reliability)
key_terms.مَذْهَبِهِ: His school of thought / theological position

ai.seo_question: Who is al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Uthman al-Sajjada and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?
ai.summary: This is a biographical entry from the book *Kitab al-Du'afa* describing the narrator al-asan ibn Ali ibn Abi Uthman. It notes his kunya, nickname, and origin, classifying him as 'weak' (da'if) in hadith transmission, with a specific note that his theological position involves 'irtifa'' (elevation or exaltation, often implying slight exaggeration or distinctiveness in belief).
